def: Tying a model's answer to supplied evidence, so it answers from the documents or tool results it was given rather than from memory.
A system declining to answer, for example because evidence or confidence is insufficient; also called selective prediction.
The share of all questions a system chooses to answer.
The error rate among only the questions a system answers, ignoring those it declines.
A plot of selective risk against coverage as the confidence threshold is lowered, showing the price of answering more questions.
A test question whose answer is not in the supplied material, used to check that a system abstains instead of guessing.
The property that among answers given a stated confidence, about that fraction are actually correct.
The average gap between stated confidence and actual accuracy across confidence bins, weighted by how many answers fall in each bin.
The entropy of a model's sampled answers after grouping them by meaning, high when the model gives arbitrary, changing answers.
A plot of stated confidence against observed accuracy in bins, where the diagonal means perfect calibration.
The confidence level below which a system declines to answer, chosen from the cost of a wrong answer and tuned on held-out data.
